observation.visible_scene: A low-angle shot taken from behind a bowling ball return rack in a green/yellow-lit alley. The rack holding several balls (orange, dark, light) sits in the foreground center and does not move; the lane gutters and the illuminated scoreboards in the background also stay fixed, indicating a static camera. A bowler wearing a yellow top, dark capri pants and white shoes is positioned on the right side of the lane.
visible_changes: At frame 1 the bowler holds a yellow ball at hip level; by frame 2 the arm has swung the ball low behind the body, and by frame 3 the ball has left the hand and is on the lane surface.

From frame 3 to about frame 13 the released ball rolls away from the foul line, moving up and to the left along the lane toward the top edge of the frame, and exits the view around frames 13-14. A dimmer blob directly beneath the ball is its mirror reflection on the glossy lane, not a second ball.

The bowler transitions from a bent-over follow-through lunge (frames 3-9) to an upright stance (frames 10 onward); as the torso straightens it rises out of the top of the frame, so only the legs remain visible for the rest of the clip.

During the upright phase the trailing foot, sole facing the camera, lifts and drifts leftward across the frame while the planted foot stays near the same spot, consistent with a weight shift or a small settling step rather than a clear walk.
The foreground rack, the other balls in it, the lane gutters and the scoreboards remain unchanged throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happens after the ball leaves the top of the frame (e.g. pinfall) is not shown.
The bowler's approach before frame 1 and their full upper body and face are outside the view.
The outcome of the throw and any later motion of the bowler beyond frame 41 are unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact release instant lies between frames 1 and 3.
Whether the leg motion in frames 14-41 is a step back or simply settling from the lunge is ambiguous.
Camera motion is treated as none; the fixed background and rack support a static shot but provide no independent depth cue.
